scope: SEZ type $28 parameters $86/$04; $83/$84 controls. Research only; no POC changes.

initialization.flags: Initializer sets +$03 bit7. Placement flags/aux bases come from original creator; $86 script sets +$04 bit1 before its first callback.

state7.aux1: Blocks of 16 moving callbacks per leg; byte zero wraps to 256 blocks. No coordinate-limit comparison.

trigger.predicate: ($6328 contact & 15)!=0; top, underside and either side all trigger
trigger.exclusions: No player-speed, state, floor, attack or platform-owner gate; platform +$03 bit7 bypasses the shared hurt/contact-bit6 gate.

timeline: If latch=0: shared overlap; no overlap returns before movement/support/counter. On overlap set latch=1.
$8662: move once using incoming X speed; compute integer X delta; support/sag/carry if player Y speed nonnegative, otherwise release support.
$8925: decrement +$30; on zero reload16 and decrement +$37; on zero reload aux1 and negate X velocity via $0437->$62F7.
After move/reversal: negative X speed selects latch2; nonnegative speed preserves latch1 but converts latch2 to0.

travel.reversal: after moving on the final callback of each leg; next callback moves in new direction
travel.stop: Final return move resets latch0. A rider still overlapping on the next callback immediately retriggers.
travel.leave: Leaving/jumping after trigger does not stop the timed excursion.
travel.terrain: No platform terrain probes or projection; objects pass through terrain. Player still receives ordinary terrain processing first.
travel.y: Y speed remains zero; only shared sag moves Y 0..8 px.

lifecycle.generic: Keepalive bit1 disables generic lifetime deletion from first state7 script entry, even before contact. Generic lifecycle still sets bit6.
lifecycle.sleep: No bit6 early return in state7/$8662: waiting trigger, movement and support still run asleep. No reinitialization on wake.
lifecycle.deletion_order: $8908 marks FE but the same callback continues; cleanup occurs in a later scheduler pass.
lifecycle.recreation: FE cleanup zeros D400[token-1] and slot; mapped recreation starts at canonical placement with counters/latch reset.

state7.presentation: Frame1 throughout; no state7-specific sound, animation or facing changes. Sag follows shared +$25 dispatcher.

state5.axis_variant_result: Sag enable only; no orthogonal movement variant.
state5.aux: Aux1 is initialized into +$34/37 but state5 does not use the travel counters.
state5.order: bit6 early-return -> signed gate $8866 -> owner/top support -> optional sag -> carry
state5.lifecycle: Generic mapped lifecycle, no script-set keepalive; sleep returns before contact/sag/release. Wake keeps existing sag fields; recreation resets them.

shared_support.owner: D3C0 is zero or this platform id; a different owner blocks support, not state7 trigger.
shared_support.speed: signed platformVy<=playerVy; state7 horizontal path is specifically playerVy>=0

carry.player_x: add integer X delta computed before reversal

shared_support.release: Shared $8843 clears mirrored side bits and releases D3C0 only if this platform owns it; sag returns toward0.
shared_support.flags: Object contact writes D521; shared merge feeds D523 on the next player pass. Support alone does not set D522 terrain-floor or change player movement flags/state.
shared_support.scheduling: Camera -> player engine/terrain -> object scheduler/contact/carry -> periodic placement scan; next player update registers landing from merged support.
shared_support.shoes: No platform-specific state or D532 selector: Spring Shoes $12/Rocket $11 use the same gate/geometry. Their player updates may supply different Y speeds or inherited flags; shared routines do not replace their state.

viewport.value: 16*aux1 travel displacement and 0..8 sag; never scale
Generic mapped create/awake/sleep/SAT bands use viewport edges; state7 keepalive exception remains
Existing post-wake retention policy may be applied explicitly where appropriate; it does not replace state7 player-distance removal. No new widescreen rule proposed.

unresolved: No remaining ROM runtime dependency for these SEZ variants. POC integration and Windows acceptance remain pending.
Whole-game evidence uses the approximate SMS harness with guarded snapshot restore; no hardware-emulation fidelity claim.

exhaustive.formula: state = 13 if (p & $7F) in (5, 11) else (p & $3F) + 1; axis flag +$25 = $FF iff p bit 7
exhaustive.evidence: CONTROLLED ROUTINE RESULT: original placement creator $80EB + two object updates for every parameter value 0..255

creator.fixture_note: Creator uses original $80EB. After script load, controlled lab restores type $28 and active flags; initial far-player $8908 deletion is excluded from initialization fields.

trigger_oracles.trigger: Pre-move closed rectangle |dx|<=24, -16<=dy<=24; any of contact bits 0..3 starts motion. No speed/floor/attack/state/owner gate.
trigger_oracles.support: Post-move triangular top test; pre-move dx is replaced by dx-1 on first motion update; relative Y speed and owner apply only to support.

state5_comparison.result: Bit 7 is the weight-sag enable, not a movement-axis selector. $04 stays fixed; $84 sags vertically 8 px and returns. Aux1 does not control state-5 movement.
state5_comparison.velocity: Both initial X/Y speeds zero, no horizontal/vertical travel oscillator; support preserves player velocities.

lifecycle.sleep: State7 sets keepalive at script entry, even before trigger. Its callback ignores bit6: motion, counters, contact and sag continue asleep. Generic lifecycle still updates bit6/SAT eligibility.
lifecycle.deletion: Original $8908 marks $FE if |platformX-playerX|>=640 OR |platformY-playerY|>=672. It then returns to the callback (not an immediate callback abort). Cleanup releases the placement token, so recreation starts from decoded origin.

signed_gate.rule: returns $FF (no support this update) iff platform Y speed > player Y speed, both signed 8.8

boundary_oracles.bounds: Counter-derived displacement, not a coordinate clamp. No terrain sampling in state7 or state5. Aux1 zero wraps to 256 blocks / 4096 updates per leg (unused by SEZ).
